summary: Completed task 4.11 (ADR-010 golden-image, byte-determinism, PNG-contract, and cross-runtime tolerance tests), including the F2 color-profile fail-closed supporting change from task 4.9 and the authorized task 4.11 EXIF orientation correctness fix with a renderer version bump. The F2 change adds SourceColorProfile/SourceColorProfileKind and the safe RenderFailureReason.UnsupportedColorProfile: an unprofiled source is treated as sRGB, a PNG iCCP/JPEG APP2 profile that SKColorSpace.CreateIcc parses is converted to sRGB by the sRGB decode destination, and a malformed/unsupported profile fails closed with no artifact. The orientation fix corrects SkiaOrientation.Apply so the dimension-swapping EXIF orientations 5-8 translate about the SOURCE dimensions (source.Height/source.Width) instead of the oriented dimensions, which had left 33-67 percent of an opaque source transparent and clipped; RenderOrientationTests proves all eight orientations are fully opaque and place two distinct corner markers in the expected quadrants, and the committed orientation golden now encodes the corrected orientation 6. RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion advanced 1 to 2 because the drawing change is output-affecting, and the committed golden manifest was regenerated (badge schema version unchanged). The golden oracle holds nine committed repository-owned synthetic decoded-pixel goldens with no writer/auto-update/auto-approval path; a substituted golden PNG and a corrupted manifest fingerprint were both verified to fail the suite. Byte determinism covers repeated renders, item identity, observation timestamp, stream chunking, and a separate fresh process. PNG-contract tests cover non-interlaced 8-bit RGB/RGBA, fixed sRGB, stripped metadata, canonical transparent-pixel RGB, straight source-alpha preservation, and profile rejection/conversion. CrossRuntimePixelComparator implements the exact canonical rule plus the 0.1 percent one-step anti-aliased-text tolerance with unguarded boundary tests, the exact canonical half runs against every golden, and the tolerant half is data-driven against an optional non-canonical golden set that is absent here. Documentation (PLANS.md 4.11 box checked plus status paragraph, README.md, docs/changelog.md, docs/implementation-readiness.md, docs/architecture.md) records the fix, version bump, counts, and non-canonical limitation. Milestone 4/Gate 4 were not marked.

known_limitations: The ADR-010 non-canonical cross-runtime tolerance half was not executed because no second non-canonical Linux runtime exists in this environment (only the pinned canonical runtime and the identical Jellyfin host runtime). The comparator and unguarded boundary tests are complete, the exact canonical half runs against every golden, and the tolerant half is data-driven against an optional Goldens/non-canonical set and skipped by NonCanonicalRuntimeFactAttribute until the second runtime is selected and its golden set supplied. Recommended resolution (recorded in docs/implementation-readiness.md and docs/changelog.md): in the testing/release milestone, select and record the second explicitly supported non-canonical Linux runtime sharing the pinned SkiaSharp 3.119.4 managed/native assets, produce its golden set with the same manifest shape, and run the ADR-010 anti-aliased-text tolerance. No result was fabricated.

The default ./build.sh test run skips 40 environment-guarded cases; the full run requires ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1 and the pinned sysroot on the loader path as recorded in docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md.

F2 defines a supported embedded profile as one SKColorSpace.CreateIcc can parse; a structurally valid profile Skia cannot represent is therefore rejected as unsupported. This is the bounded, non-guessing rule recorded in docs/implementation-readiness.md.

The orientation correctness fix advanced RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion to 2, so every output fingerprint changed even though the eight non-orientation golden PNGs stayed byte-identical; the committed manifest was regenerated for the canonical runtime.
